name: Planned Socialism
description: Publicly or collectively owned means of production, with the economy planned centrally.

name: Market Socialism
description: Publicly or collectively owned firms competing in a market, with overall planning and largely free prices.

name: Developmentalism
description: Public investment and planning to industrialize the country, protecting domestic industry while it grows.

name: Geosocialism
description: Land and natural resources belong to everyone, with their rent shared by the community and trade left open.

name: Social Liberalism
description: A market-based economy, with essential services guaranteed to all and rules that reduce inequality.

name: Pragmatism
description: No firm preference between public and private ownership, planning and markets, protection and openness: judges case by case.

name: Syndicalism
description: An economy organized by trade unions and workers' organizations, which run production and bargain for each sector.

name: Laborism
description: Defense of workers' rights and a coordinated national economy that secures jobs and income.

name: Social Democracy
description: A market economy with a strong social safety net, broad public services and income redistribution.

name: Distributism
description: Property widely spread among families and small producers, rather than concentrated in large firms or a single center.

name: Liberalism
description: Private property and free competition as the base of the economy, with clear rules and limited intervention.

name: Ordoliberalism
description: A free market within firm rules that protect competition and prevent monopolies.

name: Neoliberalism
description: Open markets, privatization, deregulation and fiscal discipline as the path to growth.

name: Liberal Developmentalism
description: Markets and private initiative drive growth, with targeted public support for industry and infrastructure.

name: Protectionism
description: Shielding domestic production from foreign competition through tariffs, quotas and preference for national goods.

name: Capitalism
description: Private ownership of the means of production, profit-seeking and prices set by supply and demand.

name: Corporatism
description: Economic sectors organized into corporations of employers and workers that negotiate and coordinate national production.

name: Austrian Liberalism
description: Free prices and individual choice, with strong private property and minimal interference in the economy.

name: Georgism
description: Private ownership of what people produce, while the rent from land and natural resources is collected for everyone's benefit.

name: Mercantilism
description: National wealth built through exports, reserves and protection of domestic production.

name: Mutualism
description: Fair exchange among producers, with cooperatives, mutual credit and property tied to use and labor.

name: Religious Traditionalism
description: Holds that faith and inherited traditions hold society together and should guide customs and laws.

name: Secular Traditionalism
description: Defends preserving inherited customs and institutions for the value they give society, without relying on religion.

name: Irreligious Traditionalism
description: Defends preserving inherited customs and traditions, and does not see religion as a moral foundation.

name: Religious Conservatism
description: Prefers gradual, cautious change in customs, with faith as the moral base.

name: Secular Conservatism
description: Prefers gradual, cautious change in customs, without leaning on religion.

name: Irreligious Conservatism
description: Prefers gradual, cautious change in customs, and gives religion no role.

name: Moderate Conservatism
description: Values established customs and institutions, but accepts change when there is a clear reason.

name: Moderate
description: No firm lean between tradition and change in customs, nor between religion and secularism.

name: Moderate Progressivism
description: Supports change in customs and individual rights, gradually and with balance.

name: Religious Progressivism
description: Supports change in customs and individual rights, with faith as part of life and values.

name: Progressivism
description: Supports change in customs and broader individual rights, with religion and public life kept separate.

name: Irreligious Progressivism
description: Supports change in customs and broader individual rights, and does not see religion as a moral foundation.

name: Religious Moderate
description: No firm lean between tradition and change in customs, with faith as an important part of life.

name: Irreligious Moderate
description: No firm lean between tradition and change in customs, and does not see religion as a moral foundation.

name: Autocracy
description: Power concentrated in one person or group, without free elections or institutional limits.

name: Anarchism
description: Society organized without a central government, through voluntary agreements and self-management.

name: Minarchism
description: Public power reduced to the minimum: security, justice and defense, and nothing more.

name: Democracy
description: Government chosen by free elections, with guaranteed rights and limits on power.

name: Councils
description: Decisions made by councils of workers and communities, elected from the bottom up.

name: Absolute Monarchism
description: A monarch with total, inherited power and no constitutional limits.

name: Constitutional Monarchism
description: A monarch with a symbolic or limited role, within a constitution and a parliament.

name: Technocracy
description: Decisions led by experts and technical knowledge rather than political contests.

name: Federalism
description: Power divided between a central government and self-governing regions.

name: Confederalism
description: Sovereign regions or peoples joined by a pact, with a weak center.

name: Municipalism
description: The most important political decisions rest with cities and local communities.

name: Neocameralism
description: Territory run like a company, with a board answerable to shareholders.

name: Aristocracy
description: Rule by an elite chosen by birth, tradition or recognized merit.

name: Dictatorship of the Proletariat
description: Political power held in a centralized way by the working class, to transform the economy.

name: Communism
description: A classless society with collective ownership, led by a party or movement.

name: Political Neutrality
description: Mixed positions, with no dominant political pattern across structure, representation and power.

name: Theocracy
description: Government run by religious leaders or religious law.

name: Security Democracy
description: Free elections combined with a strong central power and an emphasis on order and security.

name: Libertarian Monarchism
description: Favors a monarch or hereditary order, with strong private property and minimal public power.

name: Government Corporation
description: Small territories run like technology companies, with a strong executive and no elections, competing for residents.

name: Imperialism
description: Expanding the country's influence or control over other territories and peoples, by force and by politics.

name: Expansionism
description: Widening the country's territory or sphere of influence, with heavy use of military power.

name: Nationalism
description: Priority to the interests and sovereignty of one's own nation, including in trade with other countries.

name: Political Realism
description: Relations between countries are guided by interest and power, not by ideals.

name: Armed Neutrality
description: Staying out of other people's wars while keeping strong armed forces to defend one's own territory.

name: Neutrality
description: No firm lean between force and diplomacy, nor between acting abroad or staying out.

name: Pacifism
description: Rejects war and military force as a means, putting peace and negotiation first.

name: Internationalism
description: Cooperation among countries through shared institutions and agreements, with open trade.

name: Isolationism
description: Keeping the country out of foreign alliances and conflicts, and protected in trade.

name: Humanitarian Interventionism
description: Acting abroad, including with force, to stop serious abuses and protect populations.

name: Primitivism
description: Rejects industrial and modern technology, favoring a life close to nature and on a small scale.

name: Naturalism
description: Prefers natural solutions and a life in harmony with nature, using technology only when needed.

name: Environmentalism
description: Accepts technology as long as it is limited by environmental protection.

name: Technological Caution
description: Accepts new technologies, but with caution, rules and attention to risks.

name: Technological Balance
description: No firm lean between trusting technology more or nature more.

name: Technological Modernism
description: Technology is the way to improve life and solve collective problems.

name: Industrialism
description: Values industry and large-scale production as the basis of progress.

name: Technological Optimism
description: Trusts that technology will solve most human and environmental problems.

name: Futurism
description: Orients society toward the future, prioritizing innovation and fast technological change.

name: Accelerationism
description: Advocates speeding up technological advance as much as possible, even if it deeply transforms society.

name: Cosmopolitanism
description: Sees humanity as one community, with open borders and free movement of people.

name: Multiculturalism
description: Values several cultures living in the same country, each keeping its own traditions.

name: Pluralism
description: Accepts cultural diversity within rules and values shared by all.

name: Civic Integration
description: Newcomers integrate through law, language and citizenship, while keeping their customs in private life.

name: Balance
description: No firm lean between preserving the national culture and welcoming diversity.

name: Cultural Integration
description: Newcomers should largely adopt the country's culture, language and customs.

name: Assimilationism
description: Newcomers should fully assimilate into the national culture, leaving their original one behind.

name: Cultural Preservationism
description: Prioritizes preserving the existing national culture, with firm limits on immigration.

name: Ethnic Nationalism
description: The nation is defined by common origin and ancestry, and immigration should be tightly restricted.

name: Authoritarian Federalism
description: Power divided among regions, but with strong authority and little individual freedom at every level of government.

name: Moderate Democracy
description: Government chosen in elections, with limited participation and attention to order and stability.

name: Strong Government
description: A strong central government, with limited representation and an emphasis on security and order.

name: Central Democracy
description: Free elections and broad freedoms, with decisions concentrated in a central government.

name: Internationalist Socialism
description: Collective ownership and economic planning, with cooperation and open trade among peoples.

name: Protectionist Capitalism
description: Private ownership and free markets at home, with national production shielded from foreign competition.

name: Dirigisme
description: A mix of private ownership and central coordination of the economy, with national plans and protection of domestic production.

name: Cultural Traditionalism
description: Defends preserving inherited traditions and customs, seeing religion more as cultural heritage than as faith.

name: Irreligious Moderate Progressivism
description: Supports gradual change in customs and individual rights, and does not see religion as a moral foundation.

name: Secular Moderate
description: No firm lean between tradition and change in customs, keeping religion out of public life.

name: Non-Alignment
description: Staying out of power blocs, keeping an independent foreign policy and relations with many countries.

name: Non-Interventionism
description: Not interfering in other countries' affairs, avoiding wars and involvements beyond one's own borders.

name: Militarism
description: Strong armed forces and priority to military power in foreign policy, without necessarily seeking expansion.

name: Direct Democracy
description: Important decisions made directly by citizens through plebiscites and referendums, with power decentralized.

name: Moderate Free Market
description: Prices and competition set by the market, with mixed ownership and moderate openness to foreign trade.

name: Collectivism
description: Economic ownership and decisions in the hands of the community, with moderate planning and open trade.

name: Pragmatic Liberalism
description: The market as the base of the economy, with practical rules and adjustments as circumstances require, and moderate trade openness.

name: Social Libertarianism
description: Free prices and very open trade, with mixed ownership and concern for social justice.

name: National Liberalism
description: Free markets and private property, with moderate trade openness and priority to the nation's own interests.

name: Moderate Diplomacy
description: Prefers cooperation among countries, accepting limited, negotiated action abroad.

name: Defensive Militarism
description: Keeps strong armed forces to defend its own territory and interests, without seeking expansion.

name: Religious Moderate Conservatism
description: Values tradition and faith as the base of customs, but accepts gradual change.

name: Secular Moderate Progressivism
description: Supports gradual change in customs and individual rights, with religion kept separate from public life.

name: Developmentalist Authoritarianism
description: Centralized power, closed to political competition, used to direct the economy and the country's modernization.

name: Social Democracy
description: Free elections with attention to social rights and reducing inequality, with a more active central government.

name: Mixed Authoritarianism
description: Strong authority and little political competition, with power shared between the center and the regions.
